definitions.gloss: (of pets or children) to have an accident
definitions.explanation: (of pets or children) to have an accident; to soil oneself

examples.japanese: {粗相|そそう}のないようにお{願|ねが}いします。
examples.english: Please be careful not to make any mistakes.

examples.japanese: {大事|だいじ}な{席|せき}で{粗相|そそう}をしてしまった。
examples.english: I made a blunder at an important occasion.

examples.japanese: お{客様|きゃくさま}に{粗相|そそう}があってはならない。
examples.english: We must not make any mistakes with our customers.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもがトイレに{間|ま}に{合|あ}わず{粗相|そそう}をした。
examples.english: The child didn't make it to the bathroom in time and had an accident.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}が{部屋|へや}の{中|なか}で{粗相|そそう}をした。
examples.english: The dog had an accident in the room.

examples.japanese: {子猫|こねこ}が{粗相|そそう}をしないようにトイレの{場所|ばしょ}を{覚|おぼ}えさせた。
examples.english: I trained the kitten to remember where the litter box is so it won't have accidents.

notes:
{粗相|そそう} has two main uses.

Sense 1 (blunder/mishap):
Used in formal or polite contexts to refer to careless mistakes, especially in hospitality or service situations.
- {粗相|そそう}をする (to make a blunder)
- {粗相|そそう}のないように (to ensure no mistakes)

Sense 2 (toileting accident):
A euphemistic way to describe when a child or pet soils themselves or has a bathroom accident indoors.
- {粗相|そそう}をする (to have an accident)
- {粗相|そそう}をしないように (to not have accidents)

REGISTER: Formal/polite for sense 1; neutral euphemism for sense 2.
